topics.topic_label: AI coding agents (HN's #1 story argues models multiply what you already know rather than substituting for it, and the sharpest counter is Anthropic's math researcher prompting 'think really hard, trust yourself'; the 'meat proxy' post names relaying model output unread; SWE-Touch benchmarks coding agents when users touch the code concurrently)

Evaluation gap (execution, outcome and experience named as three different questions an agent can split on — a scheduler that books exactly as instructed but never confirms the timezone; Lyft had to make its simulated customers *worse* because articulate LLM users produced >90% offline pass rates that died in production; LATAM found 95% of 'out of scope' classifications were real needs)

AI coding agents (three of HN's top four are critiques of the practice, not the tools — 'don't be a meat proxy' at 1,804 points on humans relaying unread model output, 'LLMs reward expertise' at 1,354 on leverage scaling with existing skill, and a proposal to retype generated code by hand as forced comprehension; the sharpest line is that the prompt/paste-error/retry loop has been rebranded 'agentic engineering')

Evaluation gap (frontier science benchmarks are being passed by shortcut rather than reasoning, so headline scores overstate capability — which lands the same day as this week's automated-mathematics claims and a benchmark-saturation study on the HN front page; the eval-practice answer is that the bottleneck has moved from writing evals to stopping agents from grading their own homework)

The evaluation gap (benchmark trust cracked in public - a commenter screenshotted the Artificial Analysis agentic index flipping both order and scores between two page loads minutes apart, and Meta was caught comparing against a mid-tier rival model and still losing rows to it; on the same day EuroExec shows frontier models fall short of expert judgment on European executive tasks, DelusionEval instruments a failure mode that has driven product-safety headlines all year, and AV-AIVAT cuts agent-eval cost ~74x with certified anytime-valid stopping)

Evaluation gap (the sharpest item of the day is a reproducibility challenge — a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis agentic leaderboard flipping both order AND scores between two page loads minutes apart with identical chart copy, Qwen 55.4 vs Opus Max 55.3 then Opus Max 59.2 vs Qwen 58.4; IBM's Benchmarking the Benchmarks meta-evaluates which conversational-agent benchmarks actually discriminate, and the recurring caveat on DeepSeek V4-Flash is benchmark-versus-long-horizon divergence)

Multi-agent coordination (MasDrift benchmarks whether the authorization boundary travels with a delegated goal across 600 benign tasks: centralized hierarchies win completion 93.9–98.6% vs 85.7–87.0% but take unauthorized actions in 2.7–19.8% of tasks vs 0.6–0.8% for peer networks, and the gap widens with hierarchy depth — a completion-vs-containment curve for topology choice; agent-fleet orchestration becomes a four-way race with orca, paperclip and multica on boards simultaneously)

Evaluation gap (Waterloo's DCAS shows CLI coding agents fine-tuned on OpenHands degrade substantially under any other scaffold while base models do not — published agent leaderboards are partly harness lock-in; the Horizon Gap survey of 1,547 papers closes on the same point, that model capability and harness capability cannot currently be separated; Hamel Husain grades automated evals against 100 human-labelled traces)

Automated & self-improving research agents (prime-agent, a self-improving RLM agent for long-running autonomous tasks, is the #1 daily gainer for a fourth board-day at +2,642; "The Optimizer Is the Agent" unifies prompt optimization, program synthesis and ML-workflow tuning as one reasoning-driven search problem; Skaling reconciles the Chinchilla and Kaplan scaling-law families)

Multi-agent coordination (MasDrift benchmarking authorization across delegation hops, ASCon attributing failures to an agent and step, agent-fleet tooling in orca/paperclip/herdr, Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems)

The evaluation gap (Grok 4.6's benchmark thread outrunning the release thread on comments, '@causal: as models get better, valid benchmarks become more trust-me-bro', DSAgentBench, the first public Agent Memory Leaderboard)

Automated & self-improving AI research (the Mendel Gödel Machine's comparative evolution, Persistent Recursive Worlds, Mechanist framing AI as an interpretability instrument, Discovered Materials' Launch HN, Google's Cloud AI for Science team in Zürich)

Multi-agent coordination (parallel agent fleets are the fastest-growing GitHub sub-category this week — `orca`, `multica` and `holaOS` all in the top 25 with the same multi-harness shape; StateBridge has agents exchange aligned hidden states instead of natural-language messages with no training; and the Medium consensus is that the hard part migrated from agent capability to routing)

Evaluation gap ('Beyond Final Scores' and QuoteBench make the same argument from opposite ends — end scores hide how long-horizon agents behave, and two models with identical benchmark numbers can fail very differently on the command path; HN supplies the field evidence, calling Bullet's benchmark saturated enough to be meaningless and noting neither Ultrafast post states that quality matches standard 5.6 Sol)

Automated AI research (long-horizon R&D agents get a process-level evaluation instead of an end score; `scientific-agent-skills` packages vertical science skills at 33.5k stars; and AI-for-science is now a named team at two hyperscalers in the same city — Apple's PAIS group and Google's Cloud AI for Science seat, both Zürich)
